title: erica mackayana subsp. andevalensis
intro:
Erica mackayana subsp. andevalensis, commonly known as the Andevalo Heath, is a subspecies of the Erica mackayana plant, a type of flowering plant in the heath family (Ericaceae). This plant is prized for its potential health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, helping to protect against cell damage and reduce inflammation in the body. The therapeutic actions of Erica mackayana subsp. andevalensis include antimicrobial and antiseptic properties, making it useful for wound healing and skin protection. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.

Note: More research is needed to confirm the health benefits, therapeutic actions, and bioactive constituents of Erica mackayana subsp. andevalensis.
